title: Keeping Violent Offenders Off Our Streets Act of 2025
official_title: To amend title 18, United States Code, to prohibit fraud in connection with posting bail.
summary: This bill adds the posting of monetary bail, criminal bail bonds, and federal immigration bail bonds to the federal definition of the "business of insurance" under 18 U.S.C. 1033 — making organizations that post bail, including charitable bail funds, subject to the federal criminal fraud and embezzlement provisions that apply to the business of insurance.
brief: Expands the federal definition of "business of insurance" to include bail-posting activity, subjecting charitable bail funds and bail bond companies to federal insurance fraud law.

top_lines.headline: Bail Redefined as Insurance Activity
subs: Adds posting of monetary bail, criminal bail bonds, and federal immigration bail bonds to the federal definition of "business of insurance"
Subjects bail-posting entities — including charitable bail organizations — to federal criminal fraud and embezzlement provisions that apply to insurance companies

likelihoodReason: The bill passed the House 243-179 with 33 crossover votes — some bipartisan support, but the mechanism (reclassifying bail-posting entities as insurance companies) remains a partisan flash point. In the Senate, 60 votes are needed to clear a filibuster. Most Democratic senators are expected to oppose a provision that would subject charitable bail funds to federal criminal liability, and no Senate companion bill has been identified.

items.main: Names the Act the “Keeping Violent Offenders Off Our Streets Act”.
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 2 — Fraud in Connection with Posting Bail

items.main: Amends 18 U.S.C. 1033(f)(1)(A) to add "the posting of monetary bail, criminal bail bonds, and Federal immigration bail bonds" to the existing definition of the business of insurance.
items.detail: Under 18 U.S.C. 1033, persons engaged in the business of insurance are subject to federal criminal penalties for embezzlement, false statements, and related fraud. After this amendment, entities that post bail — including charitable bail organizations — are subject to those federal criminal provisions.

underreported.summary: The amendment to 18 U.S.C. 1033(f)(1)(A) extends the federal insurance fraud criminal statute to bail-posting entities. Officers, directors, and employees of organizations that post bail could face federal criminal liability for embezzlement or false statements under 1033 — not limited to bail posted for violent offenders.
underreported.why_unreported: The bill title references violent offenders, but the operative amendment applies to all bail posting without any offense-type limitation. The mechanism operates through the insurance fraud statute, making the primary legal effect a reclassification that triggers criminal exposure rather than a direct restriction on bail practices.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Menefee
featured_quotes.text: I was proud to defend that consent decree. Let's be clear about what this is. If somebody is a threat to the community, they should be in jail, regardless of whether they have a billion dollars or a thousand dollars. If they are not a threat to the community, they should not be left to languish in jail, potentially lose their livelihood, their family, all so we can make cash bail companies more rich. We should be about protecting the community, not protecting industry.

gaps: The bill amends the "business of insurance" definition but specifies no threshold — in frequency, dollar amount, or organizational structure — at which a bail-posting entity crosses into engaging in the "business" of insurance versus making an occasional bail payment.

The amendment covers criminal bail bonds and federal immigration bail bonds but does not address civil immigration bonds maintained under a separate regulatory regime, which are not referenced in the amendment text.

modified: 18 U.S.C. 1033(f)(1)(A) — definition of "business of insurance" expanded to include the posting of monetary bail, criminal bail bonds, and federal immigration bail bonds
